answer: Persistent neighbor-set retention: each agent’s history of distinct counterparties is hashed into a slow-moving trust score. A new identity starts where the network’s coldest region sits, like a glacier’s edge, so it must transact with many unrelated agents to reach normal visibility. Sybil clusters fail because their members mostly touch each other. An attacker must rent diverse, real counterparties for each fake identity, and each rental costs more than a lotus opening one petal at a time. Overlapping clusters get flagged and the whole group must re-forge its neighborhood from scratch.
